items.title: When Hollywood stopped trusting directors...
items.author: FilmStack
items.content:
<article>It’s June 1980, and director Michael Cimino is finally showing United Artists the first cut of Heaven’s Gate.

By then, the western was already a disaster. It was nearly four times over budget, almost a year late, and had one of the most notorious productions in Hollywood history. But maybe it was all  worth it. 

Before the screening started, Cimino warned them the final version might be fifteen minutes shorter.

Then they sat there for five hours and twenty-five minutes, watching a film that would ;be torn apart by critics, would humiliate United Artists, and change how Hollywood looked at directors.

This is the story of when Hollywood stopped trusting directors. This is Heaven’s Gate.

Chapters:
00:00 - Intro
00:41 - The Fuse Was Lit
05:36 - The Movie That Couldn’t Be Stopped
11:30 - Ain't No Going Back

Heaven's Gate. Michael Cimino. 70s Movies. New Hollywood. The Deer Hunter. Christopher Walken. Isabelle Huppert. Kris Kristofferson. United Artists. Best Picture Winner. Best Director Winner. Biggest Film Flops. Western Films.

items.title: JOHN CARROLL LYNCH - Actor / Director
items.content:
SEASON 2 - EPISODE 207 John Carroll Lynch - Actor / Director

In this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with actor and director John Carroll Lynch (BALLARD, LUCKY, FARGO). During our conversation, John tells us what originally drew him into acting, and we discuss an actor's function and place in film, television, and the theatre. As an actor, John has been directed by filmmakers ranging from Clint Eastwood to David Fincher to Ethan and Joel Coen (Season 1, Episode 33), and we discuss how he adapts to different methods of working. We later spend much of the episode discussing John's directorial debut, LUCKY, and we learn how he came to direct the film, how he worked with actor Harry Dean Stanton to develop a script based on his own life, and what it was about the film that attracted him to join in the first place. John also reflects on his experience directing the late David Lynch in the film, and we ask him what to expect in his next movie as a director. We worked with John on FARGO, and it was great catching up with him.

Recommended Viewing: LUCKY

items.title: Trivia of Terror 2: The Embarrassing
items.author: RedLetterMedia
items.content: <article>Ghouls and Globins alike! Share in the embarrassment of Trivia or Terror 2: The Embarrassing... Jay and Josh return to battle again in horror movie trivia cooked up by Mike (who knows a little about horror, but not a lot) Last time Josh lost to Jay. But even going up against Jay is admirable. You see, Jay has seen a lot of horror movies and has a really great memory. Josh has seen an equal number of horror movie, but he's been doing character voices for so long he's forgotten who he really is. Did Arnold see that movie? Or was it me? Did Morgan see that movie? Was that a dream? How did I end up in a leaky warehouse in Milwaukee with no air conditioning in the middle of summer trying to answer horror movie trivia questions. How far I've fallen. But hey, at least I'm not Mike.</article>

items.title: DAVID FORTUNE - Writer / Director
items.content:
SEASON 2 - EPISODE 206 David Fortune - Writer / Director

In this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with writer and director David Fortune, whose feature debut, COLOR BOOK, is now available to stream on Netflix. David grew up in East Atlanta, watching GOODFELLAS on repeat with his siblings, but it wasn't until a screening of BICYCLE THIEVES while studying at Moorehouse that he decided to become a filmmaker. Throughout the episode, we discuss David's winding path from film school to the making of his first feature, and we learn about the different types of fellowships and incubator programs that supported his development as a filmmaker. We also discuss the making of COLOR BOOK, and we learn how David prepared for the film, cast its leads, and built out the crew using mostly local talent from Atlanta. David also shares how much the film changed from the script to the final edit, and he reveals what inspired him to shoot the film in black and white. Plus, at the end, we learn a little about what he plans to explore in his next movie.

Recommended Viewing: COLOR BOOK

items.title: What Are Next for Star Trek?
items.author: RedLetterMedia
items.content: <article>It's been a minute since Rich and Mike talked a little Trek. Today is the day that happens again. Reports are the new season of Star Trek: Strange New Worlds has nabbed a total of 14,000 viewers per episode and that's some promising news! Starfleet Academy will be back for its' second and last season soon (Projected to receive negative views) and after that... not much Trek will happen. I think Alex Kurtzman Trek is DOA after Starfleet Academy. The new news on the block is that the two guys that made Game Night are writing a new Star Trek movie set in the way way future with zero legacy characters. Could be good? Could be promising? Probably be bad? No idea. But Mike wanted to tell Rich Evans about this and maybe speculate on where a new Trek series could go? What could it be about? Can the franchise be saved? Might bought a handful of actual costumes used on the clown show Star Trek Discovery and him and Rich put on two Klingon costumes to talk trek because they are both too fat to fit into the Starfleet jumpsuits they have. When talkin' Trek, why not do it with a little style!?</article>

items.title: CHARLEY GILLERAN - Rigging Key Grip
items.content:
SEASON 2 - EPISODE 205 Charley Gilleran - Rigging Key Grip

In this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with rigging key grip Charley Gilleran (A STAR IS BORN, BLADE RUNNER 2049, NO COUNTRY FOR OLD MEN). Charley shares why he got into rigging, what the job entails, and throughout the the episode he shares how he overcame several lighting challenges, ranging from Wallace's office in BLADE RUNNER 2049 to the Pacific Coast Highway in INTOLERABLE CRUELTY. Charley also recalls his first meeting with key grip Mitch Lillian (Season 1, Episode 27) on the streets of New York, and we learn why Charley moved to Los Angeles to continue and grow his career. Charley later reflects on the scheduling benefits of being the rigging grip on a job, and he shares how he preps for and adapts during a production to help the cinematographer execute his or her plan. We also discuss how much rigging has changed with advances in technology, and Charley offers his thoughts on the future of the film business in Los Angeles. We've worked with Charley on numerous films, and we were excited to have him on the podcast.

Recommended Viewing: HAIL, CAESAR!
